I farm only 1.5 mu, so I will keep the wheat-maize rotation on the whole plot instead of changing anything. Because some people in my family work off-farm, I will manage for steady output and low risk, not for the highest possible yield. I have 20 years of experience and I have well irrigation, so I will rely on improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed, use moderate but solid fertilizer rates, and make sure the key waterings happen on time. For wheat, I will put more attention on base fertilizer and two irrigations because that is what usually keeps yield stable for me. For summer maize, I will move fast after wheat harvest, keep labor simple, and use one irrigation with enough nitrogen to support growth. I will not overdo pesticides, but I will still make routine applications to avoid losing yield to common pests and diseases. On a small plot like mine, I would rather keep the plan practical, familiar, and dependable.
